name: Microcystin Degradation
source: Bourne et al. 1996, 2001; Harada et al. 2004; Thees 2019; Li et al. 2025
notes: DEPRECATED: Old single-pathway schema. Will be converted to multi-pathway network. Stepwise microcystin-LR degradation pathway found in most MC-degrading bacteria via the mlrABCD gene cluster. Microcystinase (mlrA) cleaves cyclic MC-LR (highly toxic) into linearized form (160× less toxic), serine hydrolase (mlrB) cleaves linear MC-LR into tetrapeptide (20× less toxic), and metalloprotease (mlrC) further degrades tetrapeptide into small fragments like ADDA. MlrD is a PTR2 family peptide transporter (membrane protein) whose exact role in MC degradation remains under investigation but likely involves transport of degradation intermediates or products.

nodes.name: microcystinase
nodes.notes: Diagnostic enzyme for microcystin degradation. Cleaves cyclic MC-LR (LD50 75 μg/kg) to linear form, reducing toxicity 160-fold (Harada et al., 2004; Thees, 2019).

nodes.name: serine hydrolase
nodes.notes: Serine hydrolase. Cleaves linear MC-LR into tetrapeptide, further reducing toxicity 20-fold (Thees, 2019).

nodes.name: metalloprotease
nodes.notes: Metalloprotease. Degrades tetrapeptide into smaller fragments such as ADDA (LD50 133× greater than cyclic MC-LR), completing detoxification (Bourne et al., 1996, 2001; Harada et al., 2004; Thees, 2019).

nodes.name: peptide transporter (PTR2 family)
nodes.notes: PTR2 family peptide transporter, likely membrane protein (Li et al., 2025, Ecotoxicology and Environmental Safety). Part of mlrABCD gene cluster found in most MC-degrading bacteria. Function in MC degradation still unclear but may transport degradation intermediates/products. REQUIREMENT STATUS UNKNOWN - marked as optional until function is better understood.

edges.notes: mlrA converts cyclic to linear MC-LR
mlrB cleaves linear MC-LR to tetrapeptide
mlrC produces small non-toxic fragments; mlrD role uncertain

scoring.notes: Pathway is present if mlrA + mlrB + mlrC are detected (core degradation pathway). mlrD is optional. mlrA is diagnostic marker.
